citation: Judd GJR, Eby C (2014) Spectral discrimination by Synanthedon myopaeformis (Lepidoptera: Sesiidae) when orienting to traps baited with sex pheromone or feeding attractants. Can Entomol 146(1):8-25.
notes: PMID not confirmed; left null. Records cover the pheromone-baited experiments 1, 4 and 5-14. Experiments 2 (phenylacetaldehyde) and 3 (grape juice) are feeding attractants and out of scope; experiment 15 (hourly catches, pheromone unitraps vs juice bottle traps, one day) has no records. Bar-chart means were read from the embedded figure images (Atlas reading, approximate). Internal inconsistencies: Fig. 4 caption says three yellow delta traps, the Methods say three all-yellow unitraps; the Discussion calls the fluorescent experiment 'experiment 2 (Fig. 2A)' (it is experiment 4) and cites Fig. 1B for the phenylacetaldehyde result (Fig. 1C); Fig. 1 caption gives 5 mL phenylacetaldehyde, the Methods 2 mL; the Discussion says clear traps catch less than yellow or green (Fig. 2B), but in experiment 4 clear differs only from yellow and in experiment 1 from neither; the text gives an 82% reduction for green funnels where Table 1 gives 83%; translucent white baskets are from AgBio in the general Methods and from Contech in experiment 13; the Methods (p. 13) call experiment 12 a test of all-green traps, but no experiment 12 trap is all-green; the Results (p. 16) say all chronologically later unitrap tests used 1 m spacing with rotation, but experiments 11-12 (2007) preceded experiments 5-6 (2008), and experiments 7 (2012) and 13 (2010) used 20 m spacing.

citation: Klun JA, Schwarz M, Leonhardt BA, Cantelo WW (1990) Sex pheromone of the female squash vine borer (Lepidoptera: Sesiidae). J Entomol Sci 25(1):64-72.
notes: No PubMed record found by DOI on 2026-10-23. The moth is Melittia cucurbitae in the paper (GBIF now Eichlinia cucurbitae). The abstract gives the effective binary as 99.7:0.3; the lures used the Table 1 proportions (68.5 and 0.1 percent, i.e. about 99.85:0.15), so the two disagree. Table 1 names compound 9 'hexadecen-1-ol acetate' with the acronym Z-9-16:OH; the abstract and the acetylation result make it the alcohol. The abstract hedges every minor compound ('probably also contained'); the Results call compounds 1, 6, 7, 8 and 10 confirmed by MS and single-numbered peaks confirmed by retention on two columns. Synanthedon acerrubri males were caught in Test 1 (totals 0, 1, 10 and 16 for treatments A to D); not recorded, the species is outside the v0.1 target and only totals are given.

citation: Kovalev BG, Tumlinson JH, Bolgar TS, Kolomoets TP, Kovalenko VM, Heath RR (1988) Isolation and identification of a component of the sex pheromone of Aegeria apiformis. Chem Nat Compd 24:113-115 (transl. of Khim Prir Soedin 1:126-128).
notes: English translation read. Aegeria apiformis = Sesia apiformis.

citation: Kwon J-H, Huh M-J, Lee D-H, Seo S-M, Park I-K (2021) Effect of pheromone blends, trap type and color on the capture of male clearwing moths, Synanthedon bicingulata (Lepidoptera: Sesiidae). Chemoecology 31(5):289-299.
notes: No PubMed record found by DOI on 2026-10-23. The headline optimum, about 4.3:5.7, is not an observation: it is the tested 4:6 lure corrected for the measured purities (0.4 x 94.18 : 0.6 x 82.8), so no record holds it. The Discussion says Yang et al. 2011 used lures containing an isomeric mixture and gave no isomeric information; Yang 2011 (Methods, p. 399) states isomeric purity above 99 percent. citation: Levi-Zada A, Ben-Yehuda S, Dunkelblum E, Gindin G, Fefer D, Protasov A, Kuznetsowa T, Manulis-Sasson S, Mendel Z (2011) Identification and field bioassays of the sex pheromone of the yellow-legged clearwing Synanthedon vespiformis (Lepidoptera: Sesiidae). Chemoecology 21(4):227-233.

The Discussion says individual components 'did not attract any males'; Table 2 shows 0.2-0.4 males per trap per week for single components.

Naka H, Inomata S, Matsuoka K, Yamamoto M, Sugie H, Tsuchida K, Arita Y, Ando T (2007) Sex pheromones of two Melittini species, Macroscelesia japona and M. longipes: identification and field attraction. J Chem Ecol 33(3):591-601.
notes: PMID 17265175 found by DOI on 2026-10-23. Table 1, Test III prints 100 ug of E2,Z13-18:OH in two rows (13.0 a and 0.3 b); the text and abstract give the best lure as 1:100 (E2,Z13-18:OH : E2,Z13-18:Ald), so the first is 10 ug (Atlas reading, recorded so; the schema cannot flag an amount as inferred, so each record's notes say it). The paper is inconsistent either way: the female gland ratio is 'roughly 1:10', which the printed 100 ug would match, yet the Discussion calls the 1:100 optimum similar to the females' blend. Table 2 heads its columns 'Touched' then 'Attracted', but the text's statements match the reverse (the 1,000:50 and 1,000:300 lures significantly above E2,Z13-18:OH alone in approaches; 1,000:50 above all in touches; about half of approaching males touched), so the first column is read as approaches (Atlas reading). The text places Test III about 4 km from the aldehyde-acetate field; the Table 1 footnote puts Tests III and IV in the same fields as Test II. Mean +- values are SD. The EAG dose-response series (Fig. 3b, d) is not recorded: it adds no compound and its doses are not lures. No M. longipes males came to traps in the M. japona tests, and no M. japona males to lures in the M. longipes habitat; not recorded (no non-target catch in the schema).

citation: Naka H, Horie Y, Mochizuki F, Vang LV, Yamamoto M, Saito T, Watarai T, Tsuchida K, Arita Y, Ando T (2008) Identification of the sex pheromone secreted by Synanthedon hector (Lepidoptera: Sesiidae). Appl Entomol Zool 43(4):467-474.
notes: No PubMed record found by DOI on 2026-10-23. The abstract labels Z3,Z13-18:OAc as I and E3,Z13-18:OAc as II (ratio 60:36:4); the Results label E3 as I and Z3 as II (36:60:4). The substance agrees; the labels are swapped. Test I: the text says the 50:50 lure caught 92 males in four traps, Table 1 gives 24.5 per trap with n = 2. The authors report that no other insects were caught in any of these field tests.

citation: Naka H, Mochizuki M, Nakada K, Do ND, Yamauchi T, Arita Y, Ando T (2010) Female sex pheromone of Glossosphecia romanovi (Lepidoptera: Sesiidae): identification and field attraction. Biosci Biotechnol Biochem 74(9):1943-1946.
notes: PMID 20834150 found by DOI on 2026-10-23. Table 2 totals do not follow from its means and trap numbers: the binary lure's means give 84 + 2 + 46 = 132 against a printed 144, the five-component lure's 122 against 130, Z3,Z13-18:OH alone 21 against 23. The five-component lure (Table 2 footnote e) holds Z3,E13-18:OH, Z3,E13-18:OAc and Z3-18:OAc, while the gland's minor compounds were E3,Z13-18:OH, E3,Z13-18:OAc and Z13-18:OH and the 3Z,13E isomers were 'undetectable'; the text says the lure added 'the three other minor components ... at the same mixing ratio as that found in the pheromone extract'. Recorded as printed. Arakawa et al. (JP patent P2009-209104A) identified Z3,Z13-18:OH, Z3,Z13-18:OAc and E3,Z13-18:OH earlier; not curated (a patent). The 2006 screening (Table 1) was one part of a larger field evaluation whose other lures are not reported.

citation: Naka H, Suzuki T, Watarai T, Horie Y, Mochizuki F, Mochizuki A, Tsuchida K, Arita Y, Ando T (2013) Identification of the sex pheromone secreted by Synanthedon tenuis (Lepidoptera: Sesiidae). Appl Entomol Zool 48:27-33.
notes: Published online 2012-11-07; printed in the 2013 volume (Crossref gives issue 1). Coordinates for the Motosu and Gifu sites are printed with N and E swapped (e.g. 136.67 N, 35.47 E). The Fig. 2 caption lists diagnostic ions (233, 206, AcOH-1) that differ from the text (219, 205, 191, AcOH+1). No PubMed record found by DOI on 2026-10-23. Tests II and III ran at the same orchards over the same dates and print the same Z3,Z13-18:OAc-alone row (10.7 +- 4.0, N = 6), so they probably share those traps (Atlas reading); the records cannot link them (no experiment_id yet). Single Z3,Z13-18:OAc lures attracted no other sesiid species (not recorded: the schema has no non-target catch).

citation: Priesner E, Dobler G, Voerman S (1986) Synergism of positional isomers in sex-attractant systems of clearwing moths (Sesiidae). Entomol Exp Appl 41:311-313.
notes: Short communication; trap means per flight season with no statistical tests; receptor-cell recordings reported as unpublished.

citation: Schwarz M, Klun JA, Leonhardt BA, Johnson DT (1983) (E,Z)-2,13-Octadecadien-1-ol acetate. A new pheromone structure for sesiid moths. Tetrahedron Lett 24(10):1007-1010.
notes: No PubMed record found by DOI on 2026-10-23. The text names a 'DB-13' column twice; note 3 lists only SP1000, SP2340 and DB-1, so DB-1 is meant (Atlas reading). Not recorded, stated without numbers: grape root borer males caught 'in low numbers' in traps baited with E,Z-2,13-18:OAc, and 'large numbers' of Synanthedon acerrubri in the same traps. The squash vine borer is called Melittia satyriniformis, a synonym of Eichlinia cucurbitae.

citation: Snow JW, Schwarz M, Klun JA (1987) The attraction of the grape root borer, Vitacea polistiformis (Harris) (Lepidoptera: Sesiidae), to (E,Z)-2,13 octadecadienyl acetate and the effects of related isomers on attraction. J Entomol Sci 22(4):371-374.
notes: No PubMed record found by DOI on 2026-10-23. An attraction study: the female identification it builds on (Schwarz et al. 1983, Tetrahedron Lett 24:1007-1010) is cited and not curated. Not recorded, stated without numbers: the 1983 single 2,13 isomers (only E,Z attracted), the 1984 binary to quaternary mixtures of the 2,13 isomers ('negative results'), and the 1986 seven-state monitoring (capture rose 4 to 50 times, unpublished). Table 1 is a series of tests over time with no analysis; the paper says so.

notes: In Japanese; read from the original. Isomers are written (Z,Z), (E,Z) etc. for the 3,13 double bonds, so (E,Z) = E3,Z13.

citation: Tumlinson JH, Yonce CE, Doolittle RE, Heath RR, Gentry CR, Mitchell ER (1974) Sex pheromones and reproductive isolation of the lesser peachtree borer and the peachtree borer. Science 185(4151):614-616.
notes: PMID 4841145 found by DOI on 2026-10-23. Calls the peachtree borer Sanninoidea exitiosa throughout. The text gives the natural S. pictipes pheromone as '120 ug, about 30 female equivalents'; the Fig. 2 legend gives '120 ng = 30 FE (LB) = 1 FE (PB)'. The internal evidence favours ng: the text's 1.2 ug = about ten S. exitiosa female equivalents agrees with the legend's 120 ng = 1 FE, and 4 ug per S. pictipes female would be implausible (Atlas reading). The IR text calls the band absent in S. exitiosa '960 cm-1' after giving the trans band as 970 cm-1. Reported without numbers and not recorded: the Z,Z-isomer and the purified natural S. exitiosa pheromone 'identical in attractiveness'; after silver-nitrate purification each isomer as attractive as its natural pheromone and not attractive to the other species; the (E,E)- and (Z,E)-isomers inactive for both; binary mixtures with the (Z,E)-isomer. Bioassay of note 8: fractions in 0.5 ml pentane poured into glass petri dishes on the ground of a peach orchard, males responding tabulated over 35 min.

citation: Voerman S, Persoons CJ, Priesner E (1984) Sex attractant for currant clearwing moth Synanthedon tipuliformis (Clerck) (Lepidoptera: Sesiidae). J Chem Ecol 10(9):1371-1376.
notes: Field screen without statistics. Two results without numbers are not recorded as observations: blank traps 'caught very few moths', and one Unitrap was 'as good as or better than' delta traps. 'Purity was estimated to be 99%'; positional isomers were not checked.

citation: Yang CY, Kim J, Kang TJ, Jeon HY (2009) Identification and field bioassays of the sex pheromone of Synanthedon haitangvora. J Chem Ecol 35(10):1197-1201.
notes: PMID 19830490 found by DOI on 2026-10-23. Double-bond positions were not located: DMDS adducts gave no diagnostic ions, so the 3,13 and 2,13 positions rest on retention indices against all four isomers of each on two columns and on sesiid precedent (Discussion). 'None of the other geometrical isomers of major components were attractive' is stated with data not shown; not recorded. No other sesiid species came to the 1:1 lure (not recorded: no non-target catch in the schema).

citation: Yang CY, Kim SJ, Lee SG (2011) Identification and field evaluation of the sex pheromone of Synanthedon bicingulata (Staudinger). J Chem Ecol 37(4):398-402.
Yang CY, Lee HS, Park CG (2012) Sex pheromone of the smaller clearwing moth Synanthedon tenuis (Butler). J Chem Ecol 38(9):1159-1162.
Zhang A, Leskey TC, Bergh JC, Walgenbach JF (2005) Sex pheromone of the dogwood borer, Synanthedon scitula. J Chem Ecol 31(10):2463-2479.
notes: PMID 16195855 found by DOI on 2026-10-23. Statistics: the Methods say log(x + 1) and REGW range tests; the Fig. 2 legend says arcsin square-root transformed proportions. Control traps caught nothing and were left out of the analyses. The 88:6:6 ternary ratio is 'estimated' without saying from which analysis; the gland extract gave 94:6 and no Z,E-3,13-ODDA. Not recorded: species specificity (about 92 and over 97 percent of moths were DWB, citing Leskey et al. 2005) and lure longevity (Table 2). The Results text (p. 2468) says only two peaks were 'deleted' where 'detected' is meant. The Discussion cites 'Figures 3 and 6' as trials where the 88:6:6 ternary was no better than the 94:6 binary, but Fig. 3 never tested 88:6:6 (it added 0.5-10 parts Z,E-3,13 to 94:6). It also calls the Z,Z/Z,E 94:6 lure 'the ternary blend', and 94:6 'the natural ratio', which holds for the gland extract only. The abstract gives the binary as Z,Z with '1-3%' E,Z-2,13-ODDA; every binary lure tested had 6 parts. Table 2 footnote c dates the 8-week exposure 18 May - 9 July 2004 in North Carolina; the text says 8 May - 9 July 2004 in Virginia.
